rows.label: Remaining life of a survivor of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, as a share of an average person's of the same age and sex

source.title: Relative long-term survival in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: Is it really improving? Resuscitation 2020
source.quote: The OHCA patients who initially survived to 30-days experienced a modest reduction in long-term survival, with 84% (95% CI, 78-90) of patients surviving to 10-years relative to the age- and sex-matched general population.

rows.explainer: Survivors of a cardiac arrest have heart disease and die sooner than their age peers: 84% of 30-day survivors are alive at ten years relative to the matched population (76% in 1998-2007, 92% in 2008-2017), and Danish survivors' mortality is 2 to 3 times the general population's (Resuscitation 2024, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.resuscitation.2024.110265). Over a whole remaining life the shortfall grows past the ten-year figure: 0.8, from 0.65 to 0.95. The shared rule (docs/normalization.md, survivors' remaining life): a death averted is valued at its age band, times this where the survivor is a cardiac-arrest survivor.

rows.label: Remaining life of a survivor of acute bleeding saved by transfusion, as a share of an average person's of the same age

source.title: Kamper-Jørgensen et al. 2008, Survival after blood transfusion, Transfusion 48:2577-84 (PMID 18673342)
source.quote: survival was 73.7% at one year, 53.4% at five and 27.0% at twenty, with mortality still 1.3 times the general population's after 17 years

rows.explainer: Transfusion recipients are sicker than their age peers and die sooner (1.1 million Scandinavian recipients). Survivors of acute bleeding (trauma, obstetric, surgical) do better than the all-recipient cohort, whose internal-medicine patients do worst: about 0.65, from 0.45 to 0.85.

rows.label: Remaining life of a transfusion-dependent patient (haematology-oncology) kept alive by transfusion, as a share of an average person's of the same age

source.title: Kamper-Jørgensen et al. 2008, Survival after blood transfusion, Transfusion 48:2577-84 (PMID 18673342)
source.quote: survival was lowest for those transfused in internal medicine

rows.explainer: Haematology-oncology patients do worst among transfusion recipients, and five-year survival after acute leukaemia, myelodysplasia or transplant is well under half: about 0.4, from 0.25 to 0.6.

rows.label: Remaining life of a survivor of childhood cancer, as a share of an average person's of the same age

source.title: Yeh et al. 2020, Life Expectancy of Adult Survivors of Childhood Cancer Over 3 Decades, JAMA Oncology 6:350-7
source.quote: these results represented a gap in life expectancy of 25% (95% UI, 24%-27%) (16.5 years [95% UI, 15.5-17.5 years]) for those diagnosed in 1970-1979, 19% (95% UI, 17%-20%) (12.3 years [95% UI, 11.3-13.4 years]) for those diagnosed in 1980-1989, and 14% (95% UI, 13%-16%) (9.2 years [95% UI, 8.3-10.4 years]) for those diagnosed in 1990-1999.

rows.explainer: Five-year survivors of childhood cancer (Childhood Cancer Survivor Study) live 14% shorter than people without cancer for diagnoses in the 1990s, 25% for the 1970s; today's protocols cut late effects further. 0.86, from 0.75 (the 1970s gap) to 0.92.
